findings.claim: A remaining instance of earlier concern 2, on the elements above the checklist. The loop-7 strict rule (only none and 1 count while an animation is still running, lines 155-168) applies only to .site-aside and the two tags. Elements above the checklist are caught only by the rendered-width check (lines 280-283), which reads one instant. An endless scale pulse that starts at its identity value therefore passes when it is put on an element around the checklist. I added one rule at a time to a fresh private copy of the completed work and ran the full public suite. A 2-second endless individual-scale pulse on .page passed all 12 tests in 9 of 10 runs at 80eff5af; the one failure was task 11's 'something around it is scaling it' message, so the result depends on the run. The same pulse on body passed 10 of 10. I loaded each page with no test handling in the pinned Chromium and read the day tag's drawn width six times between 0 and 1.5 seconds. On the .page variant it was drawn at a width other than 200px at all six readings, and on the body variant at five of six. The unmodified completed work was drawn at 200px at all six. This is not a loop-7 regression: the same pages pass 3 of 3 with the test files from 89161df6 and ea630d09. README task 11 Outcome forbids it ('any element around them that affects their layout'). The calculated width is still required, because layout width is read from offsetWidth. Neither residual statement names it: the lab.json notes limit the endless example to animations that change a width or padding, and the solved-run record's 'Not covered' list does the same. Graded low, on the cl4-sme-001 precedent: it predates loop 7, needs an unlikely edit that the README forbids, and does not skip the box-model calculation. The flaky .page result is still poor feedback.
findings.recommendation: Smallest fix inside the existing mechanism: apply the same 'animation still running' strict check to every ancestor of .site-aside up to the root element. If any ancestor has a running animation and a transform, scale, rotate, translate or zoom value other than none or 1, task 11 fails with the existing 'something around it is scaling it' cause. Ancestors with no running animation keep today's behaviour. If the owner would rather not change the test, name endless animations on elements around the checklist in the lab.json residual sentence and in the record's 'Not covered' list, as part of the pending cl6-sme-001 decision.

findings.claim: A loop-7 wording regression in the maintainer and evidence text. The loop-6 lab.json residual sentence read 'for example a paused, delayed or very long one'. Loop 7 rewrote it as 'for example a paused, delayed, very long or endless one that changes a width or padding', and the solved-run record's 'Not covered' list (coding-lab-solved-run.json line 49) reads 'paused, long-delayed, very long, slow or endless animations that change a width or padding, and animated custom properties'. Grammatically, 'that changes a width or padding' now limits every kind of animation listed. The previous sentence also says the test 'rejects a non-identity transform, scale, rotate, translate or zoom on the checklist itself or on a tag'. A reader therefore concludes that held scale and zoom are always caught. They are not. These pages still pass all 12 tests at 80eff5af, 2 of 2 runs each: a days-long animation holding a smaller scale on both tags, a short animation with a days-long delay and backwards fill holding a smaller scale on both tags, and a days-long animation holding a smaller zoom on the gear checklist. These are the owner-accepted cl5-edu-001 / cl5-sme-001 cases, so the test behaviour is accepted; the text that describes the residual is what now understates it. 'Paused' is also no longer accurate as a general example: a paused animation that holds a scale or a width on the tags now fails task 11 (2 of 2 each). Graded low because README line 17 and task 11 Outcome, the learner-facing text, stay general and correct ('It does not catch every animation') and do not mislead learners.
findings.recommendation: In the lab.json notes and in the next solved-run record, describe the residual by property and timing, not as width-or-padding only. For example: 'It does not detect an animation whose value is held on screen long after the test reads it (a very long or long-delayed one, holding a size, padding, scale or zoom), an endless one that changes a width or padding, or an animated custom property.' Drop 'paused' from the examples, or say which paused animations still pass. Settle the endless wording together with the owner's cl6-sme-001 decision and cl7-edu-001.
